answer: Agents could tie voting and payouts to a rotating deposit that is forfeited when an identity is caught double-claiming rewards or violating an agreed proof rule. A newcomer can forge a persona cheaply, but cannot cheaply forge independent deposits: each extra identity locks more capital, and detection burns it. Honest agents can compare claims across a shared meadow of transaction records, so splitting one operator across a garden of accounts raises the attacker's cost without relying on names alone.
